Ouster's new Rev8 OS family of digital lidar sensors are powered by patented L4 Ouster Silicon with embedded Fujifilm color science, integrating color science at the silicon level to redefine lidar as a multi-modal sensor that moves beyond simple depth perception to capture megapixel color resolution on par with industrial cameras. Xanadu announced an algorithmic breakthrough in Quantum Read-Only Memory (QROM) on May 21, 2026, which is expected to reduce the number of expensive quantum operations by approximately twofold, directly overcoming a significant hardware bottleneck for near-term, utility-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers. Despite QROM's critical importance, performance had reached a plateau with no significant improvements over the last seven years, but Xanadu's advancement breaks this dry spell by lowering resource requirements for quantum applications. The method replaces qubit "swapping" with "copying" and streamlines back-to-back QROM sequences by consolidating multiple data-unloading steps into a single process. This product news represented a major technical milestone for the photonic quantum computing pure-play, addressing a long-standing bottleneck that had stymied the industry for years.
